text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Various state insititutions financing small- and middle-sized enterprises may be joined under a mutual holding company, goverment officials propose.
- Possible boost in Finnish development aid is still disputed between foreign and finance ministry in budget talks.
- Budget proposal to cut state's aid to municipalities is against goverment's promises, deputy managing Timo Kietavainen of the Association of Finnish Local Authorities says. @
- Government plans to cut state construction subsidies by billions of markka, citing risk sector will overheat; proposal would interrupt repairs in many suburban areas.
- Finns have joined rage for Japanese virtual pet Tamagoutchi, demand exceeds supply.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Gains in Merita Bank stock have fattened major investors' portfolios by millions: small investors reckon they will make better profit on Merita than on state bonds. @
- Success of European economic and monetary union (EMU) is a condition for EU enlargement, says Sampsa Saralehto, deputy managing director at the Central Chamber of Commerce of Finland.
- Finnish insurance companies received insurance premium income totalling 48.6 billion markka in 1996 -- investments in private life insurances rose the most.
AAMULEHTI
- Alcohol sales monopoly of Finnish state-owned Alko could be unraveled, Ilkka Suominen, CEO of Alko says. @
- Milk prices could fall due to tightening competition in dairy sector, says CEO of Valio cooperative Matti Katvevuo.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Finnish company managers believe employment situation will improve, a job study shows.
- Report on Estonia disaster delayed at least until September; committee wants to study the report closely.
DEMARI
- Trade and industry ministry did not approve finance ministry's plans to cut its budget frame by 100 million markka, budget negotiations continue on Wednesday. @
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
